decision.reason: Neither candidate demonstrates a reliable elapsed-time benefit in the small crawl comparisons. The target single-thread local case does not improve; focused directory timings and MDN lack the required qualifying rounds.

scope.focused: Sixteen output paths per observation: sixteen fresh roots with one child each; sixteen new sibling branches beneath shared ancestors; or sixteen existing deep directories. Actual OutputDirectories root/prepare methods; setup, checks and cleanup outside timing.
scope.synthetic: Six markup documents or twelve binary inputs; 64 KiB buffered/local and 256 KiB streamed bodies; concurrency eight, two workers, default Got 16. Includes initialization, admission, crawl and disposal.
scope.mdn: Three saved HTML acquisitions, single-threaded, depth zero, network disabled; includes initialization, resource creation, replay processing and disposal.
scope.variants: Mkdir skips lstat after our successful non-recursive mkdir in cached mode. Combined adds reuse of verified ancestors through the existing parent cache. Strict checks and atomic publication rechecks remain. Combined versus mkdir is the incremental ancestor-cache comparison.
scope.counts: Separate instrumented observations count Node filesystem API calls, not OS syscalls. Their timings are excluded.
scope.control: Identical-before control runs in a fresh process. Process medians are the observation unit. Four-variant groups are excluded as a whole; no filtering by candidate performance and no extra rounds.

suites.method: Fresh process per variant per round; one process median per case. Balanced order places each variant in each position twice. Tests and benchmarks run serially.
suites.noiseRule: Four-million-operation CPU probes bracket timed observations. Five warm-ups and nine calibrations set a fixed 1.5x median threshold before the suite. Reject the whole four-variant round for a case when any measured probe exceeds the threshold. Require four qualifying rounds; no filtering by candidate outcomes and no added rounds.
